dedupe_keys.name: world bank logistics performance index lpi

description: The Logistics Performance Index is the World Bank's benchmark of trade logistics by country. Its overall score, from 1 (low) to 5 (high), reflects perceptions of the efficiency of customs clearance, the quality of trade and transport infrastructure, the ease of arranging competitively priced shipments, the quality of logistics services, the ability to track and trace consignments and the timeliness of shipments, each also published as a component score. It comes from a structured online survey of logistics professionals at multinational freight forwarders and express carriers, who rate eight overseas markets; the 2023 edition covers 139 countries and adds indicators from container tracking data, such as container import and export dwell times and the number of maritime partner economies. Coverage is global, with editions between 2007 and 2023. Access: free through the World Bank Data360 platform and World Development Indicators, with CSV files and an API, under CC BY 4.0. Caveats: the survey reflects international forwarders' experience, which may not represent traditional operators in poorer countries, and scores are perceptions, not measurements. It supports cross-country logistics and port performance comparisons, freight network model calibration and prioritisation of trade infrastructure investment, and complements the UNCTADstat maritime statistics catalogued here.
name: World Bank Logistics Performance Index (LPI)

sources.note: LPI overall 1-5; six components; survey of forwarders and express carriers rating eight markets; 2023 LPI 139 countries; limitation on traditional operators; CC BY 4.0; time periods 2007-2022 in WDI; WB_LPI_20 container import and export dwell time and maritime partner economies from shipping line tracking data
